text:
Dear Dr. Palmer,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate Emily, a 7-year-old girl who presented to my clinic for an orthopedic and developmental review. She is currently attending school and takes a daily multivitamin, with non-contributory family history and normal baseline vital signs.

On physical examination, Emily exhibits diminished motor tone. Her facial features are notable for pronounced frontal prominence, a flattened facial profile, a distinctly lengthened upper lip, and visible bulging globes with a bluish tint to her sclerae. Her palate is fully intact with no cleft, and her lower jaw is normally proportioned without micrognathia. The hair on her scalp is quite sparse. 

Her integument displays a soft, dough-like cutaneous texture, strikingly hyperelastic skin, and generalized cutaneous laxity with redundant folds. Musculoskeletal assessment reveals a significant kyphoscoliotic spinal curve alongside dislocation of the right hip and a congenital clubfoot deformity. She shows hypermobility of her major joints and hypermobile digital joints, paired with broad, spatula-shaped thumbs; however, no shortening of the metacarpals is noted. In contrast to her distal laxity, she has contractures of the intrinsic hand joints and restricted mobility at both elbows. 

Recent skeletal imaging demonstrates diffuse flattening of the vertebral bodies with anterior beaking along the vertebrae. Pelvic views reveal underdevelopment of the iliac bodies with hypertrophied femoral trochanters. Notably, her femoral heads appear well-formed with no dysplastic features, and there is no flaring of the metaphyses. Hand and wrist radiographs confirm that ossification of the carpal centers is not advanced, and the carpal bones show no fusion.

Her systemic examination, including cardiovascular and abdominal assessments, was otherwise unremarkable. Given this constellation of findings, I would appreciate your expert clinical evaluation and recommendations regarding next steps.

Sincerely,

Marcus Vance, MD  
Department of Pediatrics
